rows.title: Analysis: A rising commotion in Texas’ scattershot response to the pandemic
rows.standfirst: As Texas leaders struggle to find a balanced response to the pandemic and the lagging state economy, the suggestions for what they ought to do — friendly and hostile — are pouring in.

rows.title: Texas Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick says Dr. Anthony Fauci “doesn’t know what he’s talking about”
rows.standfirst: Fauci and other top medical leaders have flagged Texas as a COVID-19 hot spot, but Patrick said the infectious disease doctor has “been wrong every time on every issue.”

rows.title: After 17 youths test positive for the coronavirus, Texas juvenile lockups to begin mass testing
rows.standfirst: The agency will use the same self-administered, oral tests used to conduct mass testing in Texas’ adult prison facilities.

rows.title: Federal judge strikes down Trump asylum rule targeting Central Americans
rows.standfirst: The ruling is a defeat for the government, but it’s unclear what immediate impact it will have during the ongoing pandemic.

rows.title: Austin City Limits music festival canceled for 2020 because of coronavirus
rows.standfirst: In 2018, the festival contributed $264.6 million to the city’s economy and created or sustained at least 1,500 jobs across bars and restaurants, hotels and transportation, according to the Austin-American Statesman.

rows.title: Texas sales tax revenue declined 6.5% versus last June as state reopened for business
rows.standfirst: While collections from restaurants were depressed, Comptroller Glenn Hegar said that take-out and delivery sales, along with online purchases, helped buoy revenue in the restaurant and retail sectors.

rows.title: Internal messages reveal crisis at Houston hospitals as coronavirus cases surge
rows.standfirst: Texas was one of the first states in the nation to ease social distancing mandates. In Houston, the number of patients hospitalized with COVID-19 has quadrupled since Memorial Day. “It’s time to be alarmed,” one expert said.

rows.title: Immigration judges sue Trump administration alleging their free speech rights have been violated
rows.standfirst: The lawsuit cites a 2020 Department of Justice policy that prohibits judges from speaking about policy or law, even in their personal capacities.

rows.title: TribCast: Early voting begins as coronavirus surges in Texas and a debate over sex ed curriculum
rows.standfirst: In this edition of TribCast, Emma talks to Matthew, Aliyya and Ross about the state’s latest efforts to mitigate spread of the new coronavirus, and the State Board of Education’s ongoing debate over Texas’ sex ed curriculum.

rows.title: Upcoming Texas bar exam has law students, deans asking for in-person testing to be scrapped
rows.standfirst: The Board of Law Examiners recommended Thursday that the Texas Supreme Court cancel both the July and September bar exams and schedule an online, October exam instead. The high court is expected to make the final decision Thursday afternoon.

rows.title: Republican runoff in battleground congressional district turns explosive with focus on sex trafficking in Fort Bend County
rows.standfirst: Kathaleen Wall has run multiple television ads arguing her opponent, Fort Bend County Sheriff Troy Nehls, has not taken sex trafficking seriously. Nehls has vehemently rejected that assertion.

rows.title: More than 300 children in Texas day cares have caught COVID-19, and the numbers are rising
rows.standfirst: Nationwide, coronavirus transmission rates among children have appeared to be low, partly explaining the push to reopen schools. But Texas day cares are seeing cases increase quickly.

rows.title: Vanilla Ice cancels Fourth of July weekend concert near Austin as coronavirus cases surge
rows.standfirst: Plans for the concert drew outrage due to public health warnings that large gatherings can accelerate the spread of the coronavirus. But as of Wednesday night, only 84 tickets had been sold.

rows.title: Texas won’t specify where hospital beds are available as coronavirus cases hit record highs
rows.standfirst: As coronavirus caseloads soar across Texas, hospitals are seeing a surge of new patients. But getting information on which hospitals are hardest hit is nearly impossible.

rows.title: High school coaches’ convention will draw thousands to San Antonio as pandemic rages across Texas
rows.standfirst: To stop the spread of the new coronavirus in Texas, Gov. Greg Abbott closed bars and banned nonessential surgeries in counties that are hot spots. But indoor conventions that will draw thousands of people are still moving forward.

rows.title: He built a privately funded border wall. It’s already at risk of falling down if not fixed.
rows.standfirst: Trump supporters funded a private border wall on the banks of the Rio Grande, helping the builder secure $1.7 billion in federal contracts. Now the “Lamborghini” of border walls is in danger of falling into the river if nothing is done, experts say.

rows.title: Number of Texans filing for unemployment benefits increases by 7% over previous week
rows.standfirst: For the past two months, the number of people filing claims in Texas has trended downward. But last week, the number of people who filed for claims increased 7% over the previous week.

rows.title: Watch: Texas’ police use-of-force tactics scrutinized after George Floyd protests
rows.standfirst: The Texas Tribune spoke to criminologists, policy makers and advocates to hear their perspectives on what the current moment means for Texas and what happens next.

rows.title: Donald Trump holds narrow lead over Joe Biden in Texas, UT poll finds
rows.standfirst: President Donald Trump would beat former Vice President Joe Biden in Texas by 4 percentage points if the election were held today, according to a new poll from the University of Texas and the Texas Politics Project.

rows.title: U.S. Supreme Court won’t fast-track Texas Democrats’ bid to expand mail-in voting during pandemic
rows.standfirst: The order Thursday leaves in place Texas’ more restrictive regulations for the upcoming July 14 runoff. But the case could return to the high court before November’s general election.

rows.title: MJ Hegar maintains big fundraising lead over Royce West in U.S. Senate runoff
rows.standfirst: Hegar had her biggest fundraising quarter yet as she reaches the end of the Democratic primary runoff to challenge Republican incumbent John Cornyn.

rows.title: Analysis: With a wingman like Dan Patrick, who needs critics?
rows.standfirst: While Gov. Greg Abbott has been responding to the twin crises on his plate, Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick’s been stirring the pot — at the governor’s expense.

rows.title: Austin police will no longer cite or arrest people for possessing small amounts of marijuana
rows.standfirst: The police chief announced the policy change Thursday, more than a year after the Texas Legislature legalized hemp and complicated marijuana prosecution throughout the state.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott orders Texans in most counties to wear masks in public
rows.standfirst: Abbott previously resisted calls for such an order and at one point banned local governments from requiring masks. First-time violators will be issued a warning, though repeat offenders could be fined up to $250.

rows.title: “How many more are coming?” What it’s like inside hospitals as coronavirus grips Texas’ Rio Grande Valley
rows.standfirst: The surge in coronavirus cases has slammed hospitals in the Rio Grande Valley. Additional wards have opened. Doctors and nurses pull extra shifts. And the stream of sick people, some gasping for air, keeps growing.

rows.title: Texas GOP will proceed with in-person state convention in Houston this month
rows.standfirst: In light of the decision to go forward with an in-person convention with a new mask requirement, two sponsors announced they would drop out. Houston Mayor Sylvester Turner said he was hopeful that the organization would still reconsider.

rows.title: Texas Gov. Greg Abbott’s statewide mask mandate exempts voting sites and churches
rows.standfirst: As for the voting exemption in his mask order, Abbott says it was designed to make sure Texans do not lose their right to vote “simply because they don’t have a mask.”

rows.title: How Texans behave on July Fourth will shape the next phase of the state’s coronavirus epidemic
rows.standfirst: Millions of decisions by a restive population eager to barbecue, jump in lakes and gather for fireworks could have disastrous consequences for public health. Officials are crossing their fingers, and pleading for Texans to give up a little independence.

rows.title: Donald Trump endorses Tony Gonzales to replace U.S. Rep. Will Hurd
rows.standfirst: The president intervened Friday in the Republican primary runoff to replace Hurd, picking Gonzales over Raul Reyes, who U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz endorsed days earlier.

rows.title: “Kill ’em”: Houston GOP powerbroker Steve Hotze left Greg Abbott a voicemail requesting that National Guard “shoot to kill” rioters
rows.standfirst: Hotze, a staunch critic of Abbott’s coronavirus response, left a voicemail with the governor’s chief of staff in early June with the incendiary instruction.

rows.title: Bar exam for Texas’ aspiring lawyers canceled in July due to coronavirus concerns
rows.standfirst: Following pleas from law school deans and prospective lawyers, the Texas Supreme Court has canceled the July bar exam and will plan for an in-person exam in September and an online exam in October.

rows.title: Ten out of the 12 hospitals in Texas’ Rio Grande Valley are now full
rows.standfirst: “We are now at the point of grave concern,” said the CEO of one hospital system in deep South Texas as local hospitals began diverting patients away from their emergency rooms amid a crush of COVID-19 infections.

rows.title: Ector County GOP censures Abbott over executive power amid coronavirus, state Sen. Charles Perry calls for special session
rows.standfirst: The developments came two days after Abbott announced an executive order requiring Texans to wear masks in most public places.

rows.title: How Texans celebrated July Fourth during the coronavirus pandemic
rows.standfirst: Four Texas Tribune photographers went out to see how Texans were celebrating the holiday as the new coronavirus surges and new restrictions are imposed to stem its rise. Here’s what they saw.

rows.title: Several Texas cities worry hospitals may run out of beds in two weeks or sooner
rows.standfirst: As local officials express concerns that their hospitals could be overloaded with coronavirus patients, some are urging Gov. Greg Abbott to empower local governments to issue stay-at-home orders.

rows.title: Texas universities are moving more classes online but keeping tuition the same. Students are asking if it’s worth the money.
rows.standfirst: Universities are moving forward with reopening plans for the fall semester, anxious to bring students back. But faced with online classes and an altered campus, students are questioning if college is still worth what they’re paying.

rows.title: Texans across the state march to demand justice for Fort Hood soldier Vanessa Guillén
rows.standfirst: Guillén, a 20-year-old Army specialist, went missing in April from the Central Texas Army post. Remains found last week were confirmed to be hers, her family said. Her disappearance sparked protests against the military for its handling of sexual harassment allegations.

rows.title: Texas wants $32 million in unemployment benefits back after finding 46,000 people were overpaid
rows.standfirst: The Texas Workforce Commission said that incorrect filings and fraud can lead to overpayments, but the money must be paid back even if it was the state’s mistake.

rows.title: Poll says Texans’ hopes for quick return to pre-coronavirus life are fading
rows.standfirst: Texans remain focused on the coronavirus, are less optimistic about returning to normal quickly, and their assessments of government pandemic responses have soured, according to a University of Texas/Texas Politics Project poll.

rows.title: Texas voters split on police violence protests, open to moving Confederate statues, poll finds
rows.standfirst: Long-held views on discrimination against Black people and on memorials to the Confederacy are changing in Texas, and voters are open to universal voting by mail, according to polling by the Texas Politics Project at the University of Texas.

rows.title: Nearly 6,300 Texas companies received PPP loans of more than $1 million
rows.standfirst: The federal government released the names Monday of 51,250 companies and organizations in Texas that received the loans, which were designed to keep the economy afloat during the coronavirus.

rows.title: Houston Mayor Sylvester Turner urges Texas GOP to cancel its convention
rows.standfirst: The in-person event is scheduled for next week, even as the coronavirus continues to spread through Houston.

rows.title: Texas Democrat’s congressional campaign received a PPP loan in May
rows.standfirst: Dr. Christine Eady Mann, who is in a runoff for a Central Texas seat, has already paid the loan back.

rows.title: He was supposed to be in prison less than a year. Instead, he died after catching the coronavirus.
rows.standfirst: At least 84 Texas state prisoners have died after contracting the coronavirus, including men who were serving short sentences or set to soon go home. As the death count rose, advocates unsuccessfully called on the governor and parole board for early release.

rows.title: In GOP runoffs for the Texas House, viability in November is a leading concern
rows.standfirst: Republicans are hoping to line up their best candidates with control of the lower chamber possibly up for grabs in the fall.

rows.title: State Fair of Texas canceled for 2020 because of coronavirus
rows.standfirst: More than 2.5 million people attended the fair last year. This is the event’s first cancellation since World War II.

rows.title: Masks will be mandatory in many Texas schools when they reopen this fall, education agency says
rows.standfirst: The mask requirement doesn’t apply to students younger than 10. The Texas Education Agency guidelines also require schools to post coronavirus prevention plans and encourage hand-washing.

rows.title: South Texas landowners are hoping to use President Trump’s own words against him in a new border wall lawsuit
rows.standfirst: Landowners are alleging that the construction of the barrier is driven by little more than racism and politics and is therefore unconstitutional, according to a new lawsuit.

rows.title: Pete Sessions lost his U.S. House seat in Dallas. Can he win a new one 100 miles south?
rows.standfirst: Sessions has moved to Waco for his next bid, where an eventful GOP runoff campaign against Renee Swann will likely determine who wins the seat in November.

rows.title: Texas GOP convention will happen in person — but Republican leaders will speak via video
rows.standfirst: As the state has seen a surge in coronavirus cases, calls have been growing over the past week for the party to cancel its Houston event.

rows.title: Texas Tech tests the waters for fall semester by bringing 350 students to campus for summer classes
rows.standfirst: The 30 summer classes mark the first time in-person instruction has been offered at Texas Tech since the university closed its doors in the spring. Reopening gives campus leaders a look at what a large-scale collegiate return could look like this fall.

rows.title: More than $54 million in PPP loans went to small private Texas colleges and universities
rows.standfirst: Schools said they used the money to make payroll.

rows.title: EMILY’s List adds to massive spending on behalf of MJ Hegar in Democratic runoff against Royce West
rows.standfirst: The two are competing to take on Republican U.S. Sen. John Cornyn in November. The primary runoff is Tuesday.

rows.title: Analysis: Texas Gov. Greg Abbott is lucky not to be on the 2020 ballot
rows.standfirst: The governor would face real competition if he were on the ballot this year — even in a Republican Party primary. His response to the pandemic has opened him to political attacks from the left and the right alike.

rows.title: Texas executes Billy Wardlow, who was 18 when he killed a man. Experts argued that’s too young for a death sentence.
rows.standfirst: Wardlow had asked the U.S. Supreme Court to rule that he was too young to get the Texas death penalty. His execution was the first in Texas to proceed during the pandemic as the coronavirus rages across the state.

rows.title: “It’s insane that this is not even up to me”: International students at Texas universities can’t return without in-person classes
rows.standfirst: Thousands of international students across the state stand to be affected by the latest ruling from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, which stipulates that students on certain visas must have some in-person instruction to be able to return to the country.

rows.title: Supreme Court says employers may opt out of Affordable Care Act’s birth control mandate over religious, moral objections
rows.standfirst: The court ruled on the Trump administration’s decision to expand the types of organizations that could opt out of providing cost-free access to birth control.

rows.title: Houston convention center operator cancels in-person Texas GOP meeting
rows.standfirst: The Republican Party of Texas’ in-person convention was scheduled to happen in Houston next week. Chair James Dickey has said party leaders have worked on a contingency plan to host the convention online.

rows.title: An increase in people dying at home suggests coronavirus deaths in Houston may be higher than reported
rows.standfirst: In Houston, one of the nation’s fastest-growing coronavirus hot spots, more residents are dying before they can make it to a hospital. Medical examiner data shows that an increasing number of these deaths are the result of COVID-19.

rows.title: TribCast: Mask orders, convention drama and the road ahead for reopening schools
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast, Alexa talks to Matthew, Cassi and Aliyya about the governor’s mask order, the politics of canceling political conventions and challenges ahead for reopening schools.

rows.title: Democrats zero in on health care and electability in final days of race to challenge U.S. Rep. Michael McCaul
rows.standfirst: Mike Siegel, who ran a surprisingly close race against McCaul in 2018, faces newcomer Pritesh Gandhi in a tense runoff centering on each candidate’s suitability for the general election.

rows.title: Nearly 14% of new U.S. COVID-19 cases are recorded in Texas
rows.standfirst: Texas’ coronavirus cases now make up a significantly higher proportion than its 9% share of the nation’s population.

rows.title: Texas Gov. Greg Abbott signals support as Austin weighs fines for people not wearing face masks
rows.standfirst: In a letter to Austin’s mayor, Abbott said the city’s consideration of new enforcement measures “to ensure compliance with my Executive Orders is an important step toward reducing the spread” of the coronavirus.

rows.title: After losing big on Super Tuesday, Texas progressives hope to salvage some victories in July
rows.standfirst: The left wing of the Democratic Party is hopeful voters will embrace their priorities during the pandemic and after the death of George Floyd.

rows.title: Texas parents face a frightening lack of information on coronavirus risks in child care centers
rows.standfirst: State health officials are providing little detailed information on the spread of coronavirus in Texas child care facilities, and experts aren’t sure to what extent children spread the virus.

rows.title: Number of Texans filing unemployment claims increased for second week in a row as 117,244 sought benefits
rows.standfirst: The claims — an increase of 21.4% compared with the week before — come as coronavirus infections in the state continue surging and after Gov. Greg Abbott ordered bars to close and limited restaurant operations.

rows.title: Texas bans elective surgeries in more than 100 counties as coronavirus hospitalizations keep climbing
rows.standfirst: Gov. Greg Abbott said the decision is meant to free up resources to address the pandemic. The attorney general’s office has not said the order bans abortions, an assertion that sparked a legal battle over Abbott’s earlier prohibition on elective procedures.

rows.title: Texas GOP sues Houston Mayor Sylvester Turner over canceled in-person convention
rows.standfirst: The gathering, which was expected to draw around 6,000 people, was set to happen next week in Houston.

rows.title: Free laptops, esports and tuition cuts: How one Dallas college is pivoting during the pandemic
rows.standfirst: Paul Quinn College serves more than 500 students. In a statement, university President Michael Sorrell announced measures it would take to appease students for the loss of campus resources, including a $2,000 tuition reduction.

rows.title: Eroding private border wall to get an engineering inspection just months after completion
rows.standfirst: Months after the “Lamborghini” of border walls was built along the Rio Grande, the builder agreed to an engineering inspection of his controversial structure. Experts say the wall is showing signs of erosion that threatens its stability.

rows.title: Watch: MJ Hegar, Democratic U.S. Senate candidate, discusses her policies and chances ahead of runoff election
rows.standfirst: Backed by national Democrats, Hegar will face off against state Sen. Royce West in the July 14 runoff election. But she’s already looking ahead to her strategy for winning the election in November.

rows.title: Texas reverses course, says it won’t collect overpaid unemployment benefits in instances when it was the state’s mistake
rows.standfirst: A Texas Workforce Commission spokesperson said he was previously unaware that a judicial order bars the state from recovering funds when the overpayment is the agency’s fault.

rows.title: Two major Texas counties are trimming polling locations as workers pull out over coronavirus
rows.standfirst: Gov. Greg Abbott’s decision to not require voters to wear masks is driving away some poll workers, officials say.

rows.title: Nearly 80 Texas counties have opted out of Gov. Greg Abbott’s mask order. Others refuse to enforce it.
rows.standfirst: The governor allowed counties with 20 active cases or fewer to opt out.

rows.title: County Republican parties in Texas’ GOP strongholds say Gov. Greg Abbott going too far in coronavirus response
rows.standfirst: The Republican parties in some of the state’s biggest red counties are rebuking the governor over his use of executive authority during the pandemic.

rows.title: Analysis: Skip the convention, but get ready for school
rows.standfirst: Debates about in-person political conventions and in-person public school classes revolve around the same question: Are we ready for this?

rows.title: Texas teachers caught in the middle of political battles over schools reopening
rows.standfirst: Many Texas Education Agency employees are working from home, but the agency is requiring schools to open five days a week for in-person instruction this fall. Teachers say that mandate has grave implications for their health.

rows.title: Houston hospitals are increasingly turning away new patients as coronavirus overwhelms emergency rooms
rows.standfirst: The busiest hospitals in Houston are increasingly telling emergency responders they cannot safely accept new patients as hundreds of coronavirus patients crowd emergency rooms, and hospitals scramble to open more intensive care space.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott warns if spread of COVID-19 doesn’t slow, “the next step would have to be a lockdown”
rows.standfirst: Abbott has repeated that warning multiple times in local television interviews this week.

rows.title: Fiesta San Antonio canceled for 2020 because of coronavirus
rows.standfirst: The annual festival draws in more than 3.5 million people to the city.

rows.title: Watch: Royce West, Democratic U.S. Senate candidate, on coronavirus, systemic racism and winning the Republican vote
rows.standfirst: West will face off against MJ Hegar, a retired Air Force officer, in the July 14 runoff election. “I have been in a Republican-dominated Legislature most of my public service career, but I’ve been able to get things done,” West said.

rows.title: Early frontrunner Kim Olson faces momentum from Candace Valenzuela in bid to flip GOP-held U.S. House seat
rows.standfirst: The political trajectories of the two women are set to collide Tuesday, when Democrats will pick their nominee to replace retiring U.S. Rep. Kenny Marchant, R-Coppell.

rows.title: As Texas morgues fill up, refrigerator trucks are on the way in several counties
rows.standfirst: More than 3,000 Texans have died from the coronavirus and counties are preparing for even more deaths by expanding their capacities to store bodies.

rows.title: Ted Cruz said his Nike boycott was exerting free speech, but says people boycotting Goya Foods are silencing speech
rows.standfirst: The Texas Republican is criticizing calls for a boycott because the Hispanic food company’s CEO praised President Donald Trump.

rows.title: Why one Texas bar owner joined a lawsuit against Gov. Greg Abbott
rows.standfirst: Chris Bergeron is one of more than 30 bar owners suing Gov. Greg Abbott for an executive order that effectively shuttered bars. Listen to what Bergeron had to say about the order’s impact in the weekend edition of The Brief podcast.

rows.title: A singular figure in Texas’ coronavirus response, Gov. Greg Abbott leads a state headed in an alarming direction
rows.standfirst: The coronavirus pandemic has proved a leadership test like no other for the second-term governor. He holds nearly all power over the state’s response as it careens toward crisis.

rows.title: Texas organizers and candidates hope to engage a key voting bloc in 2020: South Asian Americans
rows.standfirst: At least five Texan candidates of South Asian descent are running for county, state and federal office this year, including three who are vying to become the first Asian American congressperson from Texas.

rows.title: Feeding tubes, hallucinations and numb toes: One Texan’s battle to survive COVID-19
rows.standfirst: When pharmacist Frank Arredondo was wheeled on a stretcher into a South Texas ward for coronavirus patients in early April, his wife wondered if they would ever see each other again.

rows.title: Trump’s ban on new visas will hurt Texas universities, experts say
rows.standfirst: Universities often hire professors and researchers using H-1B visas. Experts say limiting them only makes U.S. universities less competitive internationally.

rows.title: Three Texas House runoffs give warring GOP factions chance to settle up before November
rows.standfirst: A quieter-than-usual primary season is coming down to three runoffs Tuesday. Two incumbents are fighting for reelection, and there is a fierce battle for an open seat.

rows.title: Trump says he disagreed with privately funded border wall. The builder got $1.7 billion in wall contracts from his administration.
rows.standfirst: President Donald Trump now claims this privately funded border wall in the Rio Grande Valley — touted as the “Lamborghini” of fences — was built to “make me look bad,” even though the project’s builder and funders are all Trump supporters.

rows.title: Analysis: Greg Abbott’s critics lose political clout as Texas COVID numbers climb
rows.standfirst: The governor is increasing restrictions as the coronavirus worsens in Texas, and is beset by trolls from inside his own party for doing so. But for the first time in this pandemic, he’s ignoring them.

rows.title: Donald Trump, Ted Cruz back opposing candidates in competitive GOP runoff to replace U.S. Rep. Will Hurd
rows.standfirst: As early voting got underway, Cruz shook up the TX-23 runoff by endorsing conservative underdog Raul Reyes. Three days later, Trump backed national GOP favorite Tony Gonzales.

rows.title: Texas runoff elections show stress of coronavirus pandemic on state’s voting systems
rows.standfirst: Disabled and older voters have encountered the most problems navigating mail-in balloting as they try to avoid going to polling places. In-person voting has been generally smooth so far in the low-turnout runoffs.

rows.title: Republican Party of Texas leaders opt for virtual convention after loss at state Supreme Court
rows.standfirst: An executive committee vote late Monday capped a weekslong whirlwind of controversy and legal battles over the party’s initial plans for an in-person event.

rows.title: U.S. Sen. John Cornyn’s reelection war chest grows to $14.5 million, expanding advantage over Democratic challengers
rows.standfirst: The U.S. senator’s campaign announced the numbers a day before Democratic voters select their nominee to face the Republican incumbent.

rows.title: China sanctions U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz, other officials in retaliation for U.S. sanctions
rows.standfirst: The move comes after the Trump administration sanctioned Chinese officials last week over alleged human rights abuse against ethnic and religious minority groups in Xinjiang.

rows.title: UT-Austin says it will keep “The Eyes of Texas” as school song, but will rename buildings as Black students call for change
rows.standfirst: Last month, student athletes at the University of Texas at Austin said they would forgo recruiting and donor events if campus and athletic leaders failed to implement their demands, which were aimed at supporting students of color.

rows.title: GOP officials say Harris County party chair-elect is reneging on commitment to step aside after sharing racist Facebook post
rows.standfirst: The incoming chair, Keith Nielsen, had faced calls to give up the position last month after sharing a Facebook post juxtaposing a Martin Luther King Jr. quote with a banana.

rows.title: Texas runoff 2020 results: Watch live updates here
rows.standfirst: Get all of Texas’ election results through The Texas Tribune’s coverage of the 2020 runoff races for U.S. Senate, U.S. House and the Texas Legislature.

rows.title: 6 things to watch in Texas’ primary runoff election
rows.standfirst: In the middle of a pandemic, voters will be weighing in on primary runoffs for U.S. Senate, nationally watched congressional races and a handful of seats in the Texas Legislature.

rows.title: Joaquin Castro to challenge party elders for chair of House Foreign Affairs Committee amid reckoning on foreign policy
rows.standfirst: The move will pit Castro, a four-term House member and chairman of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, against more senior colleagues in contention for the gavel: Rep. Brad Sherman of California and Rep. Gregory W. Meeks of New York.

rows.title: Donald Trump makes last-minute pitches for Tony Gonzales, Ronny Jackson in Texas congressional runoffs
rows.standfirst: The president held tele-town halls Monday night with the two candidates he has endorsed in two of Texas’ most heated Republican primary runoffs.

rows.title: Texas hospitals are running out of drugs, beds, ventilators and even staff
rows.standfirst: Many Texas hospitals are no longer accepting transfer patients in order to maintain space for a surge that’s expected to come. In some parts of the state, it’s already here.

rows.title: Thousands of Texas prisoners still have the coronavirus. More than 25% of inmates at four units are infected.
rows.standfirst: At one prison, more than 750 inmates were actively infected with the coronavirus Monday, according to the Texas Department of Criminal Justice.

rows.title: As Fort Worth voters preserve more than $85 million for police, activists vow to lobby City Hall for spending changes
rows.standfirst: Tuesday’s election comes after nationwide calls to defund police departments have gained traction in Texas as Americans demand reforms in how law enforcement officers do their jobs.

rows.title: Joe Biden to air first general-election TV ads in Texas as polls show increasingly close race against President Donald Trump
rows.standfirst: The ads address the state’s coronavirus surge, which has become dire as hospitals and morgues scramble to respond to the rising number of infections and deaths.

rows.title: In reversal, federal government will allow international students to stay in the U.S. while taking only online classes
rows.standfirst: The repeal follows outspoken criticism from universities, legal experts and higher education advocates, who deemed the rules unfairly punitive for foreign students.

rows.title: Masks, gloves and plastic shields: What voting during a pandemic looks like across Texas
rows.standfirst: This year’s primary runoff election in Texas is different from any before it. The Texas Tribune sent photographers to see what it was like.

rows.title: This asylum seeker fled to Texas to escape violence, only to test positive for coronavirus while fighting deportation
rows.standfirst: Two sisters fled Guatemala six years apart. The older sister received asylum and settled in California. The younger one was denied and is now fighting COVID-19 in an El Paso detention center.

rows.title: Texas has the highest uninsured rate in the U.S. And during the pandemic, an estimated 659,000 Texans lost their health care.
rows.standfirst: The pandemic-driven economic downturn has left more than 5.4 million Americans with no job and no insurance. Texas has one of the largest shares of this increase.

rows.title: Texas will extend time that schools will be allowed to stay online-only, Gov. Greg Abbott says
rows.standfirst: Schools had previously been told that they would need to limit online-only instruction to the first three weeks of the school year, or they’d lose state funding.

rows.title: Three Texas House incumbents — Dan Flynn, Anna Eastman and J.D. Sheffield — lose in primary runoffs
rows.standfirst: Two other incumbents — Democrats Lorraine Birabil and Harold Dutton — were also on the ballot Tuesday.

rows.title: Lani Popp defeats Robert Morrow in Texas State Board of Education runoff
rows.standfirst: Republican leaders had rallied against Morrow, who is known for his jester’s hat and his history of racist and sexist comments.

rows.title: It took a doctor’s note and mad dash to Sonic for this coronavirus sufferer to vote
rows.standfirst: Linda Harrison and her husband couldn’t go to the polls because they were diagnosed with COVID-19. A state judge rebuffed their request for help obtaining absentee ballots, so Harrison scrambled and managed to get her vote in with four minutes to spare.

rows.title: Longtime Democratic state Sen. Eddie Lucio Jr. fends off primary challenge from his left
rows.standfirst: Lucio’s race against Sara Stapleton-Barrera was among the most competitive of the primary elections for the Texas Senate, where Republicans are expected to keep their majority after the general election.

rows.title: MJ Hegar defeats Royce West in Democratic runoff for U.S. Senate
rows.standfirst: Hegar declared victory late Tuesday, but West did not concede until Wednesday morning.

rows.title: Former White House physician Ronny Jackson and former U.S. Rep. Pete Sessions win Texas congressional runoffs
rows.standfirst: Jackson and Sessions will be clear favorites in their November general election races.

rows.title: Sarah Eckhardt and Eddie Rodriguez poised for a runoff in special Texas Senate election to replace Kirk Watson
rows.standfirst: The victor will serve the remainder of Watson’s term, which ends in 2022.

rows.title: Candace Valenzuela among runoff winners as Texas congressional battleground races take shape
rows.standfirst: Other notable winners Tuesday night included Fort Bend County Sheriff Troy Nehls and Austin attorney Mike Siegel.

rows.title: Runoff elections show Texas not quite ready for November’s main event
rows.standfirst: Most in-person voting Tuesday ran smoothly, but thousands of voters who sought to vote by mail may not be heard. And returns from the secretary of state’s office were balky.

rows.title: Texas congressional candidate backed by Donald Trump remains in too-close-to-call runoff with Ted Cruz’s pick
rows.standfirst: Tony Gonzales and Raul Reyes were separated by 7 votes in unofficial results for the Republican primary runoff to replace retiring U.S. Rep. Will Hurd, R-Helotes.

rows.title: Analysis: All eyes are on Texas headed into the 2020 presidential election
rows.standfirst: With Tuesday’s midsummer primary runoffs complete, the ballots are set for the November general election — the third major event in a year already reshaped by pandemic and recession.

rows.title: Texas classrooms can stay closed this fall without losing state funding if local health officials order it
rows.standfirst: School districts won’t lose state funding if they stick with virtual classes this fall because a local health authority has mandated that classrooms remain closed.

rows.title: Julián and Joaquin Castro criticize Gov. Greg Abbott for reopening Texas too soon
rows.standfirst: Julián Castro said Abbott made three consequential mistakes: reopening the state too early, not pushing hard enough to get adequate testing or contact tracing, and banning local officials from requiring masks in the earlier months of the pandemic.

rows.title: TribCast: Election results and voting problems in the primary runoffs
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast, Alexa talks with Evan, Matthew and Alex about the results and implications of the primary runoff elections and how voting went in the first statewide election during the coronavirus pandemic.

rows.title: Texas A&M System will provide free COVID-19 tests, but it’s a mixed bag for other schools
rows.standfirst: Up to 15,000 test kits will be available per month across its 11 universities. The system has set aside $16 million to pay for the testing program.

rows.title: Trump scales back landmark environmental law, saying it will help restart the economy
rows.standfirst: Activists warn that the changes will sideline communities of color and are concerned about projects’ climate impacts.

rows.title: Texas officials scramble to provide school reopening guidelines with only weeks of summer left
rows.standfirst: Conflicting mandates pingponging between state and local officials are frustrating many parents, students and teachers trying to plan for a fall semester during a raging pandemic.

rows.title: Nearly 1 million people voted in Tuesday’s Democratic runoff. The party says it’s a sign of strength to come in November.
rows.standfirst: The nearly 6% turnout is the highest in years for a Democratic runoff, but what that means is up for debate.

rows.title: Distilleries, wineries shuttered by Gov. Greg Abbott’s bar shutdown say they should be exempted
rows.standfirst: Distillery, winery and some restaurant owners say their businesses are different from traditional bars, which Abbott closed after COVID-19 cases and hospitalizations began to climb in June.

rows.title: Spurred by Gov. Greg Abbott’s coronavirus handling, Democratic strategists launch PAC to defeat him in 2022
rows.standfirst: The group, the Beat Abbott PAC, will raise money that will benefit the eventual Democratic nominee against Abbott in 2022.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott defends mask mandate to “frustrated” delegates at Texas GOP convention
rows.standfirst: The governor began the state party convention Thursday by addressing head-on the growing discontent with his orders to contain the pandemic.

rows.title: Harris County officials recommend, not mandate, that school districts stay closed to in-person instruction until October
rows.standfirst: On Tuesday, Tarrant County joined the list of other officials, including those in Dallas, who are mandating delayed school reopening.

rows.title: Texas Gov. Greg Abbott says “there is no shutdown coming” as coronavirus cases surge
rows.standfirst: Abbott said it will take weeks to see whether his recent mask order and decision to close bars are effective in slowing the virus’ spread.

rows.title: With high-stakes election season looming, Texas GOP Chair James Dickey faces formidable opposition
rows.standfirst: Dickey is competing against Allen West, a former Florida congressman, and activist Amy Hedtke.

rows.title: UT-Austin prepared a list of scenarios that could lead to a shutdown this fall. One trigger: a student dying of COVID-19.
rows.standfirst: Other reasons UT-Austin would close include “significant actions” by the governor or other public officials, sharply diminished hospital capacity, testing shortages on campus and unmanageable, widespread clusters of cases.

rows.title: Texas GOP postpones convention a day due to technical problems
rows.standfirst: After struggling to kick off the virtual gathering Thursday, the party’s executive committee has voted to wait until Saturday to resume business, hoping it can use the time between to smooth things out.

rows.title: Texas’ June unemployment rate falls to 8.6%, but experts warn unemployment could worsen next month
rows.standfirst: Texas’ June unemployment rate fell to 8.6% — but experts say the improvement may be short-lived with recent surges in coronavirus hospitalizations and deaths.

rows.title: Trump administration waives federal regulations to expedite border construction in Rio Grande Valley
rows.standfirst: A group of advocacy organizations said the announcement is the latest in a series of ill-advised plans that will destroy environmentally sensitive areas, endangered species and historical burial sites.

rows.title: Texas attorney general says religious private schools “need not comply” with local health orders to close
rows.standfirst: On Wednesday, TEA officials confirmed that school districts wouldn’t be penalized for barring students on campuses if local health officials mandated that schools stay closed, as long as remote instruction is offered.

rows.title: Trump administration must accept new DACA applications, judge orders
rows.standfirst: The directive comes four weeks after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled against an effort to halt the program that protects more than 100,000 Texans from the immediate threat of deportation.

rows.title: Texas will allow schools to keep classrooms closed longer than previously ordered
rows.standfirst: Facing backlash from educators, parents and public health officials, the Texas Education Agency is giving schools more time before they must resume teaching students in person and allowing districts hard hit by the coronavirus to seek waivers.

rows.title: Texas GOP will stick with virtual convention, even though federal judge ruled in-person Houston event is an option
rows.standfirst: The ruling was a striking last-minute development as party officials have struggled to get a virtual gathering underway.

rows.title: Wide-ranging lawsuit claims Texas’ in-person voting rules will disenfranchise Black, Latino voters during the pandemic
rows.standfirst: Two civil rights groups and two Texas voters are asking a federal judge to require substantial changes to polling place procedures, including an across-the-board mask mandate and expanded curbside voting.

rows.title: Federal immigration officials announce plans for resuming “remain in Mexico” hearings during the coronavirus pandemic
rows.standfirst: Texas must continue to reopen safely and the U.S. Department of State and the Centers for Disease Control must lower their global health advisories before hearings resume.

rows.title: With 4 in 5 Texans living in a “red zone,” coronavirus hot spots are moving targets
rows.standfirst: Early hot spots have been eclipsed by new regions in crisis. Now that so much of Texas is battling major coronavirus outbreaks, some severely ill patients have to travel long distances to receive the care they need.

rows.title: A Texas teacher weighs schools reopening, state guidelines and the coronavirus pandemic
rows.standfirst: Darcy Vogt Williams says districts want flexibility deciding how and when to start the new school year, given the pandemic. Listen in the weekend edition of The Brief podcast.

rows.title: 85 babies under 1 year old in Nueces County have tested positive for COVID-19 since mid-March
rows.standfirst: Nueces County Medical Examiner Adel Shaker told The Texas Tribune last week that a baby boy, younger than 6 months old, tested positive for COVID-19 and died.

rows.title: Five U.S. Navy teams deploy to Rio Grande Valley, other Texas coronavirus hot spots
rows.standfirst: Doctors and nurses at local hospitals across South Texas and the Rio Grande Valley have been working a number of extra shifts as their hospitals near capacity.

rows.title: Texas GOP convention chaos prompts delegates to create a second gathering for unfinished business
rows.standfirst: The original convention still kept going overnight, though, as delegates met to vote on key leadership positions — including the state party chairmanship.

rows.title: Former Florida congressman Allen West unseats James Dickey to become Texas GOP chairman
rows.standfirst: West defeated Dickey, who was running for a second full term, early Monday morning at a tumultuous virtual state convention.

rows.title: Texas faces a looming $4.6 billion deficit, comptroller projects
rows.standfirst: The coronavirus pandemic and low oil prices are driving down projected general revenue in the state’s current budget by more than $11 billion.

rows.title: Coronavirus kills another 1,000 in Texas in just 10 days
rows.standfirst: The number of COVID-19 deaths has reached 4,000 in Texas, and public health experts say that’s an undercount because not all people who died with coronavirus symptoms were tested.

rows.title: From the Iraq War to representing Florida in Congress to Texas GOP chair: Here’s what you need to know about Allen West
rows.standfirst: West unseated Texas GOP Chair James Dickey, who has served in the role since 2017, in a vote early Monday.

rows.title: Hidalgo County judge tries slowing coronavirus, but Gov. Greg Abbott has limited his options
rows.standfirst: Hidalgo County Judge Richard Cortez issued a new shelter-at-home order Monday night, but it “has no enforcement mechanism” according to Abbott’s office.

rows.title: Facing budget shortfalls, nearly 100 Texas mayors plead with Congress for coronavirus relief funding
rows.standfirst: City leaders are asking for more spending flexibility to address the financial shortfalls caused by the pandemic.

rows.title: These “last responders” deal with the bodies as coronavirus deaths surge in the Rio Grande Valley
rows.standfirst: Funeral homes have set up temporary morgues. Crematoriums are running overtime. Families must wait more than a week to bury their loved ones. For body couriers and funeral workers, there’s no letup in sight.

rows.title: Some Texas high schools can start football, volleyball practices as soon as Aug. 3
rows.standfirst: Bigger schools — those with a 5A or 6A designation — will have to wait until September.

rows.title: Texas Supreme Court Justice Paul Green says he will retire at the end of August after 15 years on the bench
rows.standfirst: Green’s term ends Dec. 31, 2022. Gov. Greg Abbott will appoint his successor.

rows.title: Trump pushes to exclude undocumented immigrants when congressional seats are divvied up next year
rows.standfirst: If it withstands legal challenges, the memo signed Tuesday by the president could cost Texas several seats in Congress. But it’s unclear what data would be used to parse undocumented immigrants from the overall population counts.

rows.title: UT-Austin is considering only filling its stadium to 25% capacity when football resumes Sept. 5
rows.standfirst: University officials had previously said they were considering a limit of 50% to comply with social distancing guidelines.

rows.title: State Rep. Lorraine Birabil concedes after primary runoff defeat
rows.standfirst: The Dallas Democrat won a special election runoff earlier this year to finish the term of Eric Johnson, now the Dallas mayor.

rows.title: U.S. Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez accuses U.S. Rep. Roger Williams of joining in on harassment
rows.standfirst: Williams, an Austin Republican, says he didn’t hear or participate in a heated exchange involving Ocasio-Cortez and a Republican colleague.

rows.title: Analysis: Coronavirus spreads to the Texas state budget
rows.standfirst: Now that the first official estimate of the coronavirus’ effect on the Texas economy is out, the hard work starts. Legislators have to figure out which parts of the state budget to cut and which parts to keep.

rows.title: Undocumented immigrants behind on their rent are self-evicting across Texas
rows.standfirst: Without money to pay rent, facing pressures from landlords and afraid of courts, people without legal immigration status have limited options.

rows.title: Houston’s Chinese Consulate abruptly ordered to close by Trump administration
rows.standfirst: The first sign of the American order came when a Houston TV station aired video showing people in the courtyard of the consulate apparently burning documents on Tuesday night.

rows.title: Search the newly updated Government Salaries Explorer
rows.standfirst: The Texas Tribune’s database of compensation for Texas state employees has been updated to represent employee salaries as of July 1. It includes detailed data for the 113 agencies in state government and positions at each of those agencies.

rows.title: UT-Austin faces a third lawsuit claiming that white students were unfairly denied admission under affirmative action
rows.standfirst: Previous attempts to overturn UT-Austin’s admissions policies have proven unsuccessful, including a 2018 lawsuit by the same group that was dropped earlier this month and a 2016 U.S. Supreme Court case that sided with the university.

rows.title: TribCast: The post-convention state of the Texas GOP and a bleak budget forecast
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast, Alexa talks to Matthew, Cassi and Ross about the Texas GOP’s convention chaos and how the uncertainty of the coronavirus pandemic is affecting the state budget.

rows.title: Timing of Supreme Court justice’s retirement allows Gov. Greg. Abbott, not voters, to pick his two-year replacement
rows.standfirst: Aug. 21 is the deadline for vacancies that trigger a November election to fill open seats. If Green’s replacement is not on this year’s ballot, the next general election will be in November 2022. Abbott will appoint someone to fill the rest of the term.

rows.title: Travis County DA will not take Javier Ambler, Michael Ramos cases to grand jury before leaving office this year
rows.standfirst: District Attorney Margaret Moore was originally slated to present both cases to a special grand jury in August.

rows.title: As Congress feuds over unemployment payments, more than 1.6 million jobless Texans are about to lose a $600 weekly benefit
rows.standfirst: The CARES Act’s $600 weekly unemployment benefit expires in Texas on Saturday, leaving out-of-work Texans in a period of uncertainty as Congress debates what to put in new federal relief legislation.

rows.title: As school reopenings falter, some Texas parents hire private teachers. Others can only afford to cross their fingers.
rows.standfirst: With the safe reopening of schools this fall in doubt, parents with the resources are setting up “learning pods” or seeking other options. But the do-it-yourself approach to education threatens to leave behind students of color and poorer families.

rows.title: The coronavirus is keeping Texas prisoners who’ve been approved for parole behind bars
rows.standfirst: Thousands of parole-approved prisoners remain locked up during the public health crisis. The coronavirus has delayed pre-release programs and kept people set to go home inside infected prisons.

rows.title: Analysis: Texas in a state of financial uncertainty
rows.standfirst: The dire financial forecast from the Texas comptroller says a lot about the pandemic’s harsh impact on the economy. It’s based on uncertain assumptions about what will happen next — and could easily change again.

rows.title: Mask mandate appears to be helping in Texas, but experts ask Gov. Greg Abbott not to rule out a shutdown
rows.standfirst: A plateauing of new virus cases would hardly represent a victory over the pandemic, but it would help keep hospitals from being overrun with sick patients.

rows.title: Harris County orders schools closed until Sept. 8
rows.standfirst: The order could extend further, Harris County Judge Lina Hidalgo said.

rows.title: Hanna brings flooding, power outages to southern Texas Gulf Coast
rows.standfirst: A section of the Texas coast already reeling from thousands of coronavirus cases will continue to feel the effects of the storm, which was the first hurricane of the season.

rows.title: Texas Republicans face tough 2020 election after a rocky 12 months
rows.standfirst: The state’s Republicans have had to weather a monthslong series of distractions while preparing for a November election that is now clouded by President Donald Trump’s declining poll numbers and the coronavirus pandemic.

rows.title: Fort Worth 1-year-old can stay on life support, Texas appeals court rules
rows.standfirst: The 2nd Court of Appeals ruled Friday that Tinslee Lewis can stay on life support. The case, which has garnered much scrutiny, is still awaiting a final ruling.

rows.title: Ten members of this South Texas family have contracted COVID-19. She doesn’t want to be next.
rows.standfirst: Elisa Soliz, a Hidalgo County school bus driver, says she’ll retire before subjecting herself to a busload of kids, many of whom lack access to health care. Listen in the weekend edition of The Brief podcast.

rows.title: A federal prohibition against some evictions has expired. Here’s what you need to know about unpaid rent in Texas.
rows.standfirst: Many local governments have implemented their own measures to protect tenants from eviction during the pandemic, and there are groups that help tenants navigate what can be a complicated and traumatic process.

rows.title: As Hurricane Hanna makes landfall, Texas Gov. Greg Abbott warns residents to not forget coronavirus
rows.standfirst: Gov. Greg Abbott talked about hurricane preparedness and about special measures being taken because of the pandemic at a Saturday afternoon news conference.

rows.title: With 1,000 new coronavirus fatalities in Texas in just 6 days, the state’s death count is rising faster
rows.standfirst: More than 5,000 people in Texas have died from COVID-19, the disease caused by the new coronavirus, according to state health data released Sunday.

rows.title: For the first time in years, Texas Democrats running for the U.S. House have more campaign cash than Republicans
rows.standfirst: Midway through 2016, Texas Republicans had $20.9 million more for their U.S. House campaigns than Democrats. This year, Democrats have a $7.5 million advantage.

rows.title: Analysis: A Republican president wants to use the census to dilute the power of Texas, the biggest Republican state
rows.standfirst: The Trump administration wants to exclude undocumented immigrants from the population counts used to determine seats in Congress, an idea that would cut into the strength of the Texas delegation to Washington, D.C.

rows.title: Texas ranchers, activists and local officials are bracing for megadroughts brought by climate change
rows.standfirst: A new study from the University of Texas at Austin and Texas A&M University warns that droughts in the latter part of this century could be the worst on record.

rows.title: Sarah Eckhardt wins special election for Texas Senate seat after Rep. Eddie Rodriguez forgoes a runoff
rows.standfirst: Rodriguez said he would focus his efforts on helping gain a Democratic majority in the House.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott extends early voting for November election by six days, starting Oct. 13
rows.standfirst: The early voting period for the Nov. 3 election will start Oct. 13 instead of Oct. 19.

rows.title: Thousands of Texans remain without power in the aftermath of Hurricane Hanna
rows.standfirst: Gov. Greg Abbott cautioned that there will be continued threats of flash flooding even as rainfall slows.

rows.title: Texas biotech facility in College Station tapped to mass-produce potential COVID-19 vaccine
rows.standfirst: The Texas A&M University System Center for Innovation in Advanced Development and Manufacturing has a federal contract to mass-manufacture doses of a candidate COVID-19 vaccine being developed by Novavax.

rows.title: Texas fifth and eighth graders won’t have to pass STAAR test to move on to the next grade
rows.standfirst: Gov. Greg Abbott said Monday that Texas students must take the state standardized test next spring, but fifth and eighth graders can graduate without passing it.

rows.title: Texas’ count of coronavirus deaths jumps 8% after officials change the way they tally COVID-19 fatalities
rows.standfirst: Hispanic Texans are overrepresented in the state’s updated fatality count, making up 48% of deaths, but only 40% of the state’s population.

rows.title: Cecile Young to lead Texas Health and Human Services Commission
rows.standfirst: Young, a longtime public servant, will take the helm of an agency of nearly 37,000 employees as it navigates a worsening pandemic and a host of lingering internal problems.

rows.title: Austin police release footage showing the killing of Mike Ramos
rows.standfirst: The release of the video comes two days after armed protester Garrett Foster was shot and killed by an unnamed, armed driver while protesting police brutality in Austin.

rows.title: Texas families now have until Aug. 21 to apply for food aid to make up for school meals
rows.standfirst: The families of more than 20% of the 3.6 million eligible school children across the state have yet to apply for federal aid under the Pandemic EBT program.

rows.title: Trump administration says it will reject new DACA applications while weighing future of the program
rows.standfirst: Acting Secretary of Homeland Security Chad F. Wolf said that in response to the recent U.S. Supreme Court decision, officials are considering whether to fully rescind the program.

rows.title: Texas attorney general says local health authorities cannot “indiscriminately” shut down schools
rows.standfirst: After Paxton’s guidance, the Texas Education Agency reversed course and announced that the state won’t fund schools that remain closed under a local public health mandate.

rows.title: Coronavirus cases in Texas nursing homes more than doubled in July. Families say the state still isn’t testing enough.
rows.standfirst: On Monday, the state released data on COVID-19 cases in Texas nursing homes after initially arguing that the information wasn’t subject to public disclosure.

rows.title: Conservative think tank leader says schools should reopen since most Texans dying from COVID-19 are elderly or Hispanic
rows.standfirst: In an interview, Vance Ginn said the intention of his Twitter thread was to outline the more thorough data provided by the state. He also said his tweet with a GIF was “woefully taken out of context out of bad faith.”

rows.title: This Silicon Valley-based lender sued thousands of Texans during the pandemic. It stopped when we started asking questions.
rows.standfirst: The company didn’t say exactly how many pending lawsuits it would drop in Texas and elsewhere, but it confirmed that “several thousand cases” would be impacted.

rows.title: Analysis: Funding for rural broadband in Texas is in trouble. The pandemic might save it.
rows.standfirst: Rural Texans have been clamoring for high-speed internet services for years, and the requirements of a pandemic — work, schools and medicine — have raised the stakes. But a state fund that helps provide those services is in financial trouble.

rows.title: What happens when a hurricane hits a coronavirus hot spot? South Texas cities found out the hard way.
rows.standfirst: Texas’ emergency response teams have worn personal protective equipment and distributed it to residents across South Texas in responding to Hurricane Hanna, another challenge for the state as it prepares for hurricane season during the pandemic.

rows.title: U.S. Rep. Louie Gohmert, a mask skeptic, tests positive for coronavirus
rows.standfirst: Gohmert, 66, said in a televised interview that he wonders if he may have caught the virus from wearing his mask. Medical experts, however, overwhelmingly recommend masks as a means of preventing the virus.

rows.title: Baylor students must test negative for coronavirus before returning to campus this fall, officials say
rows.standfirst: The university is mailing testing kits to its 18,000 students and requiring a negative test result before allowing them back on campus.

rows.title: Young people are infecting older family members with coronavirus in multigenerational homes
rows.standfirst: The emerging trend highlights the difficulty of sheltering the most vulnerable while the young and healthy return to work and school.

rows.title: TribCast: Texas revises coronavirus death tally as school reopening chaos continues
rows.standfirst: On this week’s TribCast, Alexa talks to Ross, Aliyya and Emma about the state’s bad relationship with data and the latest pingponging guidance on how and when schools can reopen during the coronavirus pandemic.

rows.title: This private border wall was already at risk of falling down if not fixed. A hurricane made things worse.
rows.standfirst: Engineering experts said photos of damage from last weekend’s storms reinforce the idea that building and maintaining a border fence so close to the river poses serious challenges.

rows.title: Trump rallies oil and gas workers in the Permian Basin against Democrats ahead of the November election
rows.standfirst: President Donald Trump’s comments doubled as part campaign speech, part policy announcement, as polls continue to show a close competition with presumptive Democratic nominee Joe Biden in the once-solidly red state.

rows.title: At least 187 Texans received mystery seeds mailed from China. State officials warn they shouldn’t be planted.
rows.standfirst: Officials are unsure of the motive behind the unsolicited packets but suspect that they are part of an online scam.

rows.title: Texas schools are being compelled to reopen classrooms on the state’s timetable, like it or not
rows.standfirst: Gov. Greg Abbott has yet to formally announce a definitive plan for reopening Texas schools safely, but two actions Tuesday effectively force districts to have students back in classrooms after eight weeks of the school year’s start.

rows.title: Colleagues feared U.S. Rep. Louie Gohmert would catch COVID-19. Sure enough, he did.
rows.standfirst: Gohmert’s colleagues were afraid the mask-avoiding congressman from Northeast Texas might get infected with the coronavirus. On Wednesday, their fears came true.

rows.title: Across Texas and the nation, the novel coronavirus is deadlier for people of color
rows.standfirst: New data on Texas coronavirus fatalities reveals stark racial disparities.

rows.title: “It cost me everything”: Hispanic residents bear brunt of COVID-19 in Texas
rows.standfirst: Not only are Hispanic Texans catching the coronavirus at higher rates in the state’s largest county, but they also suffer some of the worst outcomes.

rows.title: Custodians, cafeteria workers and bus drivers also fear returning to Texas schools
rows.standfirst: Texas schools employ almost as many support staff members as they do teachers, often in hourly or part-time jobs with low pay. The state has offered limited guidance on how to protect them on the job.

rows.title: In a rare move, Texas Republicans tell President Trump “no” after he calls for delaying the election — something he’s not legally allowed to do
rows.standfirst: The president does not have the legal authority to move Election Day; that power resides with Congress.

rows.title: After voluntarily publishing its data, UT-Austin now has the unwelcome distinction of leading U.S. colleges in COVID-19 cases
rows.standfirst: While some universities nationwide and in Texas are still refusing to disclose coronavirus cases, UT-Austin set up a digital dashboard allowing community members to see updated student, faculty and staff cases. But the transparency has already proven to be a double-edged sword.

rows.title: For Austin officials investigating Garrett Foster’s death, a key question may be which party acted in self-defense
rows.standfirst: Comments by police officials have raised concerns about whether the department is biased against the 28-year-old man who was killed, activists and an Austin City Council member say.

rows.title: Who should prosecute the El Paso Walmart shooting suspect? A year after the massacre, local and federal prosecutors still face hard decisions
rows.standfirst: The incoming El Paso district attorney is going to inherit the biggest case in the city’s history. But the federal government is pursuing its own charges, and the new DA is weighing whether to pursue the county’s case.

rows.title: Here’s how the COVID-19 pandemic has unfolded in Texas since March
rows.standfirst: We put together a timeline of the state’s efforts to protect public health during the pandemic, and how those restrictions and provisions have changed over time.

rows.title: Analysis: President Trump’s attempt to rock the vote sends a shudder through the political world
rows.standfirst: President Donald Trump tweeted about delaying the November election, and in the process, launched an attack on whether anyone should trust the results when the votes are tallied.

rows.title: “I truly thought last Friday was gonna be my last,” says Texas lawmaker who was hospitalized for coronavirus
rows.standfirst: State Rep. Tony Tinderholt told The Texas Tribune he is recovering from a serious case of COVID-19, which he thought last week might kill him. His wife and two of his children also tested positive.

rows.title: Gov. Greg Abbott says local health officials can shut down schools only in limited circumstances
rows.standfirst: Abbott said local health authorities can’t shut down in-person instruction before school starts, but an outbreak on campus once students have arrived could prompt a closure.

rows.title: Houston announces $15 million to assist tenants, but passes on mandatory eviction grace period for people behind on rent
rows.standfirst: The city’s first program, launched in May, received overwhelming demand and ran out of funds in 90 minutes.

rows.title: U.S. Army sergeant who shot Austin protester Garrett Foster posted tweets about retaliating against demonstrators
rows.standfirst: Daniel Perry has come forward as the shooter of Garrett Foster, a 28-year-old armed demonstrator who was killed while protesting police brutality in Austin last Saturday.

rows.title: Raul Reyes seeking recount in Republican runoff against Tony Gonzales for U.S. Rep. Will Hurd’s seat
rows.standfirst: Reyes was U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz’s choice in the race. President Donald Trump backed Gonzales.
